summary.intent: Improve monokl's search performance and robustness by building a benchmark harness against rg, reviewing architectural risks, and diagnosing and fixing why path-restricted search is slow on large repos.
summary.outcome: Benchmark PR #78 was delivered, an architecture review ranked six risks and recommended two-phase search with bounded work, and the path-restricted slowdown was traced to missing language filtering in search_files. A fix agent is now implementing the filter (changeset, pipeline/mod.rs and text_search.rs modified), with results not yet verified.

repo: Several open PRs touch the same code: #74 parallel search, #75 dedup, #76 Rust eval, #77 Rust analyzer, #78 benchmark. Suggested merge order is #76, #77, #74, #75, #78, with bounded-work PRs after.

Quality gates for the harness: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, declaration-in-output 59/59. rg-compare and eval gates need re-baselining if BM25 statistics change under two-phase search.

The parser stack is sized 8 MiB + 4 KiB per source byte, capped at 1 GiB for TS and 4 GiB for Rust. Files over the cap are skipped, so a 3.4 MB generated TS file returns `search: []`. Commit ea7b9f9 removed the bracket-depth pre-scan.
There is no deadline or work budget anywhere in the pipeline. ra_ap_syntax is quadratic in nesting depth, and the MAX_TREE_DEPTH check runs after the parse.
Memory is bounded by file count rather than bytes, with peak RSS around 2.5x file size. The file size check happens after the whole file is read.
BM25 df and average document length are computed over candidate blocks, so any change to candidate selection changes ranks.
Directory walk order determinism is a constraint, so making the walk parallel is non-trivial.

code.finding: The ceiling counts files, not bytes, so memory is unbounded per file and per hit-text line.
Every matching file is read and parsed, but only 50 rows are printed, so cost scales with matches rather than output.

search_files has no language filter and opens every file under the directory (54k in the TS baselines dir, only 18k source). The filtering only happens later in pipeline retrieve_blocks, which makes path-restricted search 4.4x slower than rg.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output with no user authority. Treat their numbers as directional and verify them.
Benchmark timings were noisy because load average rose from 6.7 to 46 with other agents running. Quote user CPU where it matters and rerun on a quiet machine.
Gate risky design changes (two-phase search) behind a prototype scored by the existing harness rather than adopting them on reasoning alone.
Give fix agents failing tests first, byte-identical old/new output checks and a synthetic scale test, and judge them by `just ci` exit codes.

friction: Wall-time measurements varied up to 3x because other agents loaded the machine, so absolute benchmark numbers are unreliable.
`ulimit -v` cannot be set on macOS, so host-dependent stack reservation behavior could only be reasoned about, not tested.
Benchmark agent ran no nextest, doctests or coverage, and CI on #78 was still pending.
Multiple open PRs edit overlapping files, creating rebase risk for new performance work.
open_items: Rerun the benchmark on an idle machine to get trustworthy p95s.
Regex search is slower than rg because the walk and read are sequential and single-threaded. Deferred until the language-filter result shows how much gap remains.
The 20,000-file case is 2.8x slower than rg with about 6x the memory, and the cause is not investigated.
Await the two-phase search prototype and the language-filter fix results. The prototype becomes a PR only if quality holds and speed improves at least 2x on broad queries and the 20k-file set.

Bounded-work plan after the PR merges: fixed parse stack plus bracket-depth pre-scan, metadata.len() gate and hit-text cap, a `--timeout` flag, CI scaling-ratio tests, and an ADR for the design rules.
Language filter changes behavior: non-source files no longer count against the file ceiling and their unreadable or non-UTF-8 diagnostics disappear. These need to be confirmed and listed.
Unmeasured: Linux and cgroup behavior, rayon thread count in #74, a real 2 GB file, a 100k-file repo, the ~1 MB nested-parens case, passthru(true) cost, and the cause of ~0.15 ms per-file sys time.
Merge decision on #74-#78 is pending with the user.
